items.title: Auction market plumbs new low as buyers thin
paras: Australia’s auction market continues to plumb new lows, with clearance rates falling to their lowest level nationally since the depths of the COVID lockdowns in April 2020.
Last week’s average final clearance rate for November was only 43%, with final weekly clearance rates stuck in the 40s for 22 of the past 24 weeks.

This weekend’s preliminary auction clearance rate suggests that the market has softened further, with the national rate of 44.0% the lowest preliminary result since April 2020, well below the spring average to date of 50.4% and the winter average of 52.3%.
The preliminary result suggests the final national auction clearance rate could plunge into the low 40s, or possibly even the high 30s, once more results are gathered.
Sydney’s preliminary clearance rate fell 4.2 percentage points to 48.1%, slipping below 50% for the first time this spring and coming in below the spring average to date of 53.7%.

Melbourne’s preliminary clearance rate fell sharply to 47.8%, down 11.3 percentage points from 59.1% last week and well below the spring average to date of 54.5%. This was Melbourne’s lowest preliminary clearance rate since September 2021.

Brisbane’s preliminary clearance rate fell to just 25.3%, down 5.9 percentage points from last week and remaining well below the spring average to date of 30.3%. Brisbane’s preliminary clearance rate has remained below 30% in five of the past seven weeks.
Adelaide’s preliminary clearance rate fell to 41.3%, down 2.2 percentage points from last week and below the spring average to date of 44.2%.
Clearly, the national housing downturn remains entrenched, with values falling by 9.0% across the five main capital city markets, with each recording heavy falls:
Given the lack of buyer demand reflected above, home prices have a lot further to fall.

items.title: Author Tim Winton says Exmouth wrong place for a port
paras: Tim Winton has been advocating for Exmouth Gulf since the inception of the port proposal. ( ABC News: Courtney Bembridge )
A deepwater industrial port in a northern WA tourist town is facing a backlash from locals and conservationists.
The Exmouth Chamber of Commerce backs the plan and says it will provide plenty of benefits to the community.
If approved, construction of the port is scheduled to begin in early 2029.

A proposed deepwater industrial port in northern Western Australia has been described as unnecessary, unjustified and unacceptable by locals and conservationists worried about the impact on marine animals.

The Gascoyne Gateway Marine Complex is proposed to be built just outside of Exmouth, 1,230km north of Perth, where it will feature a single jetty wharf, bulk fuel storage, a solar farm, and a seawater desalination plant.
The port is proposed to be built 10km south of the township. ( Supplied: Gascoyne Gateway Ltd. )
The port will be designed to service cruise liners, defence and commercial supply vessels.
The proposal has caught the attention of conservationist and famous author Tim Winton who has opposed the project.
Exmouth local Brinkley Davies also said she was concerned about the port's location so close to town and World Heritage Ningaloo.
"It is worrying because it is my front yard, but also the marine ecosystem that is at risk is a major factor," Ms Davies said.
Having worked in marine conservation herself, Ms Davies has been involved in the campaign against the port since its initial proposal in 2020.
Brinkley Davies believes more people are now aware of the issues with the port. ( ABC Pilbara: Yousuf Shameel )
"It was not widely spoken about then and in the last five or six years, the town has really boomed and there is a lot more people living here and more people standing up for the place," she said.
"There are a few key species that really have an importance in this area, one of them is dugongs.

"There is a very important seagrass meadows where they are feeding and they also come in here to nurse their calves and rest, and that area is at direct risk of being covered in silt if they are going to dredge."
Signs with messages opposing the port have been placed around town. ( ABC Pilbara: Yousuf Shameel )
Fellow Exmouth local Violeta Brosig said she was concerned the port could impact the humpback whales that rely on the Gulf.
"My main concern is it is going to be right in the middle of the parts of the humpback highway in Exmouth Gulf," she said.
However, the Exmouth Chamber of Commerce president David Gillespie said it was an opportunity of a lifetime for locals and there would be flow-on benefits for the community.

"There's for and against on both sides with businesses that agree to disagree, but I just get back to what the positives are from an economic perspective and what that will do for the town, for increased housing and population."
Exmouth Gulf is now the chosen site for the Gascoyne Gateway Marine Complex. ( ABC Pilbara: Yousuf Shameel )
Gascoyne Gateway CEO Daniel Jackson said there had been extensive community consultation and believed the majority of locals and businesses were in favour of the port.

"We certainly acknowledge that there's seasonal windows, we're talking a few months of the year in which higher degree of risk mitigation is required to manage interaction between vessels and fauna, as it does now.
"There's commercial vessels operating there today that are moving in and out and around fauna in the Gulf."
The project is still undergoing approvals, with the WA Environmental Protection Authority currently undertaking public consultation.
World renowned author, conservationist and patron of Protect Ningaloo, Tim Winton, said the Exmouth Gulf was the wrong place for a port.

"It is one of the world's most important humpback whale nurseries and the idea of building a wharf a kilometre long into the whale refuge and to bring up to 600 vessels a year into the whale nursery just seems fundamentally wrong," Mr Winton said.
"We're of the view that this is unnecessary, unjustified and unacceptable in its impacts to the Ningaloo estate."
While this proposal could be approved by and started by 2029, the Exmouth Gulf is also being considered for National Heritage Listing, with that decision not expected until 2030.
The WA government is also looking to establish a new marine park covering the entire Exmouth Gulf.
Exmouth Gulf is also currently undergoing an assessment to be added to National Heritage List. ( Supplied: Australian Marine Conservation Society )
"Exmouth Gulf, is about to become a marine park, it is currently being assessed for national heritage status, which is obviously a pathway to world heritage protection," Mr Winton said.
Protect Ningaloo has so far gathered over 74,000 signatures for their submission to the EPA.

Mr Jackson said a large portion of the environmental review submission focused on dredging during the construction phase and it would be done in a controlled manner to ensure the seabed was not overly disturbed.
If approved, construction on the port is expected to begin in 2029 and be operational by end of that year.

items.title: A slowing economy could mean higher youth unemployment, economist warns
paras: Lachlan Riddell says he has applied for hundreds of jobs over the past three years. ( ABC News: Kate Nickels )
Economists are watching to see if youth unemployment rises further as the economy softens.
Young people are increasingly competing with multiple job holders for work.
University students are being encouraged to engage with the job market well before they graduate.
Young people struggling to find work can be the canary in the coal mine for the rest of the jobs market.
And a recent rise in the youth unemployment rate could be a sign of things to come.
Australian Bureau of Statistics data from September showed youth unemployment at 11.1 per cent compared with the overall unemployment rate of 4.7 per cent.
While still lower than before the pandemic, a slowing economy could mean youth unemployment rises further in the coming months.
"We tend to see younger workers affected more heavily when there is a slowdown," chief economist at jobs website SEEK, Blair Chapman, said.
Commonwealth Bank economist Harry Ottley said the youth unemployment rate was "definitely rising more quickly than other cohorts".
Lachlan Riddell has experienced what he describes as "job hunting depression".
"I started to fall into a bit of a slump, [asking myself], 'why am I even doing this'," he said.
The 24-year-old estimated he had applied for hundreds of jobs over the past three years, from collecting supermarket trolleys to retail and hospitality roles.
"I feel like there is a mentality that … generation Z don't want to work, that they're very selective about what they want to do, which is simply not true," he said.
Lachlan Riddell says without a permanent job, he's struggling to make ends meet. ( ABC News: Kate Nickels )
Mr Riddell has a Diploma of Music and works casually as an audio-visual technician, but shifts are sporadic.
He said that despite having wide-ranging work experience, he rarely received a response from employers, and most job applications were online.
He has concerns that success in Tasmania's small jobs market can depend less on what you know than who you know.
Lachlan Riddell has applied for jobs, including in hospitality. ( ABC News: Sam Ikin )
As he continues his search for more permanent work, Mr Riddell said he was struggling to make ends meet on his Jobseeker payment and relied on support from his fiancee.
Graduate job ads have been trending down after post-pandemic highs, according to SEEK.
"There is anecdotal evidence that several larger firms have reduced their graduate intakes in recent years," Mr Chapman said.
"The big four accounting firms are a good example of this as they reduced their intakes in response to declines in demand."
Blair Chapman says the number of graduate jobs has been trending down. ( ABC News: John Gunn )
He said he suspected a slowdown in demand for graduates would continue in Australia as the economy softened.
The rise in youth unemployment has come alongside continued job growth for young people.
Harry Ottley says there are more young people in the labour market looking for work. ( Supplied )

"The share of young people in work [the employment-to-population ratio] is 63.6 per cent, down from a peak of 66.7 per cent in November 2022, but well above its 2019 average of 59.7 per cent," Mr Ottley said.
He said youth participation was also high at 71.4 per cent compared with 67.7 per cent in 2019.
Blair Chapman says younger workers are often more heavily affected when there is an economic slowdown. ( ABC News: Jake Grant )
There have been fears that the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) could lead to a jobs apocalypse, particularly for young people and white-collar workers.
But a study by the Department of Employment and Workplace Relations found the technology was not yet causing broad disruption to Australia's labour market.

The study, released in July this year, also found that jobs for people aged 20 to 24 had grown slightly faster than those for people aged 25 and over since the introduction of ChatGPT, while young graduate outcomes remained resilient.

But the report did cite evidence from the US suggesting young people have experienced slower employment growth than older people since the introduction of generative AI tools, especially in occupations more exposed to AI.
Qantas last week announced 850 job cuts and plans to accelerate its use of AI.
"We do think there'll be some job disruption at the margin, let's say, over the next five years," Mr Ottley said.
Federal Skills and Training Minister Andrew Giles said AI was mostly augmenting jobs, "so changing the way in which a job is done rather than completely automating a job".
"We've got to really focus on our skill to make sure workers are equipped to manage this transition," Mr Giles said.
Young people are also facing increasing competition for positions from existing job holders.

items.title: Carers of people with disability left exhausted navigating NDIS
paras: Amanda Solarino has been left stressed trying to secure more NDIS support for her son Alex. ( Supplied: Amanda Solarino )
Caregivers of people with disabilities say navigating the NDIS to try to get more support for their loved ones is leaving them feeling exhausted and taking a toll on their mental health.
It comes as accessing the NDIS becomes increasingly difficult, after cuts in funding for some sectors began to be rolled out on October 1.
Amanda Solarino, who lives in Romsey just outside Melbourne, is the full-time carer for her 21-year-old son Alex, who is autistic, non‑verbal and has an intellectual disability.
Ms Solarino said she was continuously replacing furniture and fixing walls as a result of her son's escalating aggression, and she struggled to get the help she needed from the NDIS.
Some of the damage caused by Alex at home. ( Supplied: Amanda Solarino )
"Alex's aggression isn't just directed at us or the furniture anymore — he's now turning it on Erica, his 19‑year‑old sister," she said.
"She's so anxious she won't walk down the hallway unless she knows exactly where he is."
Amanda Solarino lives with several health conditions herself. ( Supplied: Amanda Solarino )
"No one's paying to fix the furniture he breaks ... the $2,000 couch he breaks with his head or the two beds he's broken in the last 18 months," she said.

Ms Solarino said Alex had been kicked out of programmes providing day care in their area, and in a neighbouring town, leaving the family with one support worker who can only come for six hours every Monday.
Ms Solarino has had to plaster the walls after Alex damaged them. ( Supplied: Amanda Solarino )
The stress is affecting Ms Solarino. She has chronic migraine disorder and requires injections every 12 weeks, and her arthritis has worsened.
"They're suspecting autoimmune problems, probably brought on by all the stress," she said.
After Alex's aggression worsened, the NDIS escalated his housing request to crisis level and eventually approved his specialist disability accommodation.
Ms Solarino said the new plan did not fulfil the provisions she had asked for, but she was too exhausted by the process to fight it.
She said all she wanted for Alex was for him to live with some dignity.
On the Sunshine Coast, the family of Breanna Medcalfe, a 24-year-old law student with a spinal injury and quadriplegia, has also faced challenges getting the NDIS help she needs.
Ms Medcalfe is completely paralysed from the neck down and relies on assistance for all activities, including driving and showering.
Breanna Medcalfe now relies on her parents for care. ( ABC News: Josh Dye )
Ms Medcalfe has one support worker, but mainly relies on her 60-year-old parents to take care of her daily care responsibilities.
She would like more NDIS-funded support hours, but her requests have been declined.
"Because I have mum and dad and I live at home with them, they are like my informal supports, and they therefore can provide the main support, which is incorrect," she said.
"We haven't yet come to the point where we've run out of support hours, but we've been very restricted as to what we can do," she said.
"Why do we have to justify that we're disabled enough to need this funding?"
Ms Medcalfe says its not right that her parents have to care for her all the time. ( ABC News: Josh Dye )
The NDIS refused to answer specific questions about supports provided by family members and the lack of resources in regional areas, referring the ABC to its website.

A spokesperson defended the agency's role in providing "critical, essential services" and confirmed that funding resets for social, economic and community participation and improved daily living supports had gradually rolled out from October 1.

The spokesperson said supports vital to the health, safety, and wellbeing of participants would be excluded from the changes, and added that new safeguards will protect participants with 24-hour care needs.
Ms Medcalfe and her support worker Katy-Lea Holmes. ( ABC News: Josh Dye )
Ms Medcalfe says she wants the NDIS to understand the real‑world consequences of its decisions.

items.title: US investigators say too soon to know what caused tanker-cruise ship collision
paras: All 197 passengers and crew on the American Heritage cruise ship and tanker survived the collision. ( AP )
The US National Transport Board has begun investigation a collision between a tanker and cruise ship in New Orleans on Friday, local time.
All 197 passengers and crew on the American Heritage cruise ship and tanker survived the collision.
The investigation will include a team of 16 people, who will hand out a preliminary report in 30 days, and final report in 18 to 24 months.
The US National Transport Safety Board (NTSB) says it is on a "fact finding" mission to figure out how a tanker collided with a cruise ship that had more than 100 passengers.
All 197 passengers and crew on the American Heritage cruise ship and tanker survived the collision in New Orleans on Friday, local time.
Officials said 32 people were taken to hospital, including two police officers thrown into the Mississippi River when the boat rolled, but none of the injuries were critical.
The National Transportation Safety Board said the tanker's voyage data recorder had been recovered, and a 16-member team would spend a week in New Orleans investigating the incident.
NTSB member John DeLeeuw said the agency expected to release a preliminary report within 24 to 30 days, with the final investigation report expected in 18 to 24 months.

“We are still in the fact-finding stage. We look at the maintenance record, the history of the ship. We actually look at a number of things, but it is way too soon [to know what happened]," Mr DeLeeuw said.
The first warning Joe Knab, a passenger on the American Heritage cruise ship, had of the imminent collision was the tanker blasting its horn several times.
The hit was hard, and the cruise ship immediately started leaning. The crew quickly gathered everyone on the third deck, got them in life vests and started getting them off the boat.
But the vessel suddenly rolled and sent Mr Knab and about 100 other passengers and crew into the muddy Mississippi River.
Tugboat operators, other cruise ship captains, nearby workers, police and other rescuers rushed to help.
"It's fine now, but it was a little scary there at the time," Mr Knab told WDSU-TV, still in the jeans he was wearing on the boat, now covered in mud.
Emergency services help people out of the water after a tanker crashed into a cruise ship in New Orleans. ( AP: Devon Flanagan )
Mr Knab was wearing a shirt from a Hilton hotel where the passengers gathered after the incident. The rest of his belongings were in the river but somehow his phone still worked.
He said he was in the water for about 15 minutes, and joked that his 20 years in the navy likely helped him.
A lawsuit, filed by the Board of Commissioners of the Port of New Orleans, said the Atlantic Asphalt tanker caused at least $US1 million ($1.47 million) in damage to its terminal.
A judge issued a warrant on Friday giving federal officials control of the ship for now.

The tanker has been towed away from the site, but it could take weeks to move the cruise ship, which remains on its side against a terminal in the Mississippi River, Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham told reporters on Saturday.
Emergency crews work at the scene of the collision. ( The Advocate via AP: Enan Chediak )
She said the first step was to make sure the 60,500 litres of fuel on the boat were removed safely.
Traffic has been limited on the Mississippi River, but Captain Burnham said boats should be able to move both upstream and downstream soon.

items.title: Ocean that once covered Flinders Ranges preserved Earth's earliest life
paras: Chace Range in the Flinders Ranges has unusual rock formations that indicate the presence of submarine canyons. ( Supplied: Adelaide University )
New research has painted a clearer picture of the ancient Flinders Ranges landscape and early fossil formations.
Unusual rock formations were found to be evidence of canyons formed underwater.
The area is included in an ongoing bid for UNESCO World Heritage status.
Researchers have found new evidence about how ancient sea level changes led to the preservation of some of Earth's earliest complex life forms.

Geological features across South Australia's Flinders Ranges were mapped in the study led by Adelaide University, reconstructing the landscape of hundreds of millions of years ago to investigate how sediment and fossils came to be.
"You have to imagine that the Flinders Ranges … was under the ocean," University of Adelaide associate professor Diego Garcia-Bellido said.
Researchers say the findings give a clearer picture of how the Flinders Ranges landscape changed. ( Supplied: Adelaide University )
"Canyons were being carved and creating this accommodation space for a lot more sediment."
The findings focused on the Ediacaran period, about 550 million years ago, "at the time or just before the appearance of the first complex life on the planet".
Diego Garcia-Bellido works at Chace Range in September. ( Supplied: Xavier Damiani/Adelaide University )
Looking at Nilpena Ediacara National Park in the Flinders Ranges, researchers noticed unusual rock formations that indicated the presence of submarine canyons.
Dr Garcia-Bellido and his colleagues from the university and the South Australian Museum began finding the canyons "all over the Flinders", up to 280 metres deep and 6 kilometres wide.
The findings suggest that flooding of seawater played a crucial part in the formation of the canyons, and subsequently the preservation of some of the first complex life on the planet.
Knowledge about how the canyons formed could help with the understanding of early evolution.
"The environment is a very important point of reference; you need to know where these organisms started living, and why they settled there," Dr Garcia-Bellido said.
Karol Faehnrich and Jim Gehling map the geological features in the Flinders Ranges in 2024. ( Supplied: Diego Garcia-Bellido )
"What we see is that, as the canyons get filled and the sea level rises, this creates in the shallow shelf an environment that is ideal for the shallow water microbial mat to grow.
Fossils of early soft-bodied organisms known as Ediacaran biota were first discovered in the Flinders Ranges in 1946
Fossils like these form an important part of an ongoing bid for UNESCO World Heritage recognition for the Flinders Ranges.
Jim Gehling does some mapping at Chace Range in 2016. ( Supplied: Diego Garcia-Bellido )
"The fact that this is so important is because we see how animals arrive on this planet, or start developing on this planet," Dr Garcia-Bellido said.
"With these studies, we're trying to find more about these very earliest complex forms.
"It's glimpsing a world that is probably the most alien we can actually find because we've gone so far back in time that the animals that we see around us today … didn't even exist."

items.title: All Blacks suffer 73-year first in defeat to Wales
paras: Wales beat the All Blacks for the first time since 1953. ( Getty Images: Michael Steele )
Wales has ended a 73-year winless sequence against New Zealand with a stunning 35-28 victory in the Nations Championship.

Wales, who last overcame the All Blacks in 1953 and have endured a dismal recent run, outscored the visitors five tries to four on Saturday and produced a defensive performance for the ages to end a run of 34 losses to the three-times world champions.

They caught New Zealand cold with two early tries and two more at the start of the second half, and heroic Welsh defence resisted waves of attacks in the closing stages to hold on for a famous victory.
"It's come from belief. Obviously, we've got the crowd behind us, and the energy and the noise was unbelievable," Welsh man of the match James Botham said.
"We've been training on the defensive side of things, and it shows how training has come on and just how much we have got each other's back."

The Wales players team were in tears at the end amid raucous celebrations at Cardiff's Principality Stadium after Tomos Williams, Dewi Lake, Archie Griffin, Eddie James and Louis Rees-Zammit scored tries and Sam Costelow was immaculate with the boot.
New Zealand were stunned, held up over the line three times in the closing minutes at a raucous Cardiff. ( Getty Images: Dan Istitene )

New Zealand's tries were scored by Cortez Ratima, Wallace Sititi, Fehi Fineanganofo and Peter Lakai, all converted by Richie Mo'unga, but were held up over the line three times, with the Welsh defenders making a total of 346 tackles by the end of the game.
It was only the fourth time Wales had beaten New Zealand in 39 meetings.
"A hell of a defensive effort from them," New Zealand coach Dave Rennie said.

One consolation for the All Blacks is that the bonus points they have picked up have put them above South Africa in the Northern Hemisphere standings as they seek a place in the new competition's final at Twickenham.
Elsewhere, England thrashed Eddie Jones's Japan 78-15 Nations Championship at Twickenham, with England winger Will Joseph scoring a record-equalling five tries.

Joseph was making only his second appearance for England, more than four years after his debut, and started his return with a try from his first touch inside the opening 65 seconds before adding three more in the first 25 minutes.
The 24-year-old scored a fifth after the interval to equal the record set by Rory Underwood in 1989 and matched by Josh Lewsey in 2003 and Henry Arundell at the last World Cup.
England ran in 13 tries in a record score against Japan, and in the new Nations Championship competition.
And in Genoa, Argentina beat Italy 19-14, condemning the hosts to their fifth defeat in five matches in the competition.

items.title: Reserve Bank of India imposes monetary penalty on One Mobikwik Systems Limited
paras: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has, by an order dated November 06, 2026, imposed a monetary penalty of ₹9.00 lakh (Rupees Nine Lakh only) on One Mobikwik Systems Limited (the company) for non-compliance with certain provisions of the directions issued by RBI on ‘Prepaid Payment lnstruments (PPIs)’ and ‘Fraud reporting’. This penalty has been imposed in exercise of powers conferred on RBI under the provisions of section 30(1) read with section 26(6) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. The statutory inspection of the company was conducted by RBI with reference to its operations for the period from June 2025 to March 2026. Based on supervisory findings of non-compliance with RBI directions and related correspondence in that regard, a notice was issued to the company advising it to show cause as to why penalty should not be imposed on it for its failure to comply with the said RBI directions. After considering the company’s reply to the notice, additional submissions made by it and oral submissions made during the personal hearing, RBI found that the following charges against the company were sustained, warranting imposition of monetary penalty: the company had allowed fund transfer by certain PPI holders to non-pre-registered beneficiaries beyond the prescribed limit. the company failed to report certain frauds within the prescribed timeline. The action is based on deficiencies in regulatory compliance and is not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the company with its customers. Further, imposition of monetary penalty is without prejudice to any other action that may be initiated by RBI against the company. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1496

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "India matters most for future of planet" says British High Commissioner Lindy Cameron
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): In recent times when climate change has become a pressing issue with countries across the world being ravaged due to climate catastrophes, it becomes imperative to discuss and deliberate upon global actions that can help the world rise up and meet these challenges. At the NDTV World Summit's a discussion was held on the theme, "India Matters The Most For Future Of Planet". Participants in the discussion included Erik Solheim, Former Minister of Climate and the Environment of Norway; Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India; Shishir Priyadarshi, President Chintan Research Foundation; Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative. "India is the country that matters the most for the future of the planet and climate change. India's ambition for development should not in any way be constrained by the responsibilities of the planet," Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India, emphasised. She noted that the UK is committed towards the Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) reforms, technology and research support in India to aid the efforts. "Every dollar invested in resilient infrastructure pays 4 times over," said Cameron. "Lived experience of climate emergencies helps people to understand why their government needs to take policy action now," she added. Further talking about the need for urgent government action, Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative said, "Series of disasters affecting both developed and developing countries are serving as a wake-up call. As rich countries will get more and more affected by climate change which they did not imagine till a couple of years ago, most vulnerable countries are going to be struggling with impacts who also have very less capacity to deal with it. India is taking a leadership role in the global fight against climate change. Initiatives such as Global Biofuels Alliance, International Solar Alliance, and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure are some efforts taken by India in recent years to manage the climate crisis. (ANI)

items.title: India is the top market for investment globally: Mark Mobius
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Mark Mobius, Founder of Mobius Capital Partners LLP , and an ace investor with expertise in emerging markets said, India's is the top stock market globally where he would like to invest. In an exclusive interview with ANI, the octagenarian said, "India would have to come first when I think about investment," Mobius stated, "Of course, India would have to be the first choice. Then, I would probably look at Taiwan. It's a Chinese society, but it's a free society and they're doing very well. Now we're beginning to see China rise again. There will be some interesting companies in China, but still, India remains our top pick." Mobius highlighted technology as his favorite sector to invest in India. "In the future, I believe there's going to be significant growth in hardware technology. As you know, India is already strong in software technology, but moving forward, hardware manufacturing will gain momentum here in India," he said. Discussing India's semiconductor infrastructure, Mobius mentioned that it is already developing. "Many of the world's large semiconductor companies already have software development operations in India, employing thousands of software engineers. The next step, of course, is hardware. Soon, we'll see large semiconductor manufacturing plants. The scale of investment we're talking about isn't in the millions, but billions of dollars, to produce the most advanced semiconductors in the world." Mobius also fondly remembered Ratan Tata, who passed away this month. "I met him many years ago and found him to be a very friendly, humble, and insightful person. I was deeply saddened to hear about his passing. I considered him one of the great Indian entrepreneurs of the century," Mobius added. Earlier on Monday, Mark Mobius, speaking at the NDTV World Summit 2024, reiterated he was bullish on India's real estate and semiconductor sectors, as he outlined the potential of these two key industries. In the semiconductor space, he said fabrication companies (fabs) will come here because India has got the population and the labour force. The octagenarian believes India will become "the leader" of the semiconductor industry. The government has so far approved five semiconductor units in India, of which construction in two sites is on, and soon the work in the other three will start. The companies have already made a cumulative investment of almost Rs 1.5 lakh crore. While talking about the parameters he looks at while investing in companies, Mobius said he looks at the growth of earnings in companies, along with the return on capital invested, and the quality of management. Asked about his investment advice to his "younger self," Mobius said, "Don't be in a rush, and study carefully". He added that one has to listen to the market. (ANI)

items.title: Mukka Proteins Limited Announces Rs 98 Crore Preferential Issue for Acquisition and Expansion
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel VMPL Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: Mukka Proteins Limited , India's largest fish meal and insect meal producer and a leader in the animal protein industry , has announced the approval of a preferential issue worth Rs 98 crore by its Board of Directors. This strategic move will help Mukka Proteins in its ongoing domestic and international acquisition and expansion efforts, reinforcing its position in the global market. A significant portion of the funding will come from the promoter and promoter group, underlining their commitment to the company's robust growth strategy. The preferential issue will comprise up to 1.96 crore equity shares at Rs50 per share, aggregating to Rs98 crore. This price includes a premium of Rs49 per share on the face value of Rs1. Mukka Proteins will use the raised capital to enhance production capabilities and meet the growing global demand for sustainable and high-quality protein solutions, particularly in the fishmeal and insect meal sectors. In a clear show of confidence, Mukka Proteins' promoters have committed to a capital infusion of INR 60 crore through a preferential allotment of equity shares. This significant financial backing will be used to strengthen the company's financial position, reduce debt, and fund key operational improvements. Mukka Proteins has consistently embraced sustainability, having commercialized insect protein as a significant innovation for the aquaculture and animal feed industry. The company's waste-to-food initiatives have contributed to environmental sustainability, particularly in collaboration with the Mangaluru municipality for waste management. These efforts not only align with global environmental best practices but also enhance circular economy processes, focusing on converting municipal waste into valuable protein and oil products. Mukka Proteins is known for its strong commitment to ecological preservation, evident through the development of sustainable products such as fishmeal, fish oil, and insect protein. As a key player in the aquaculture and nutraceutical markets, Mukka contributes 25-30% of the market share in India's fishmeal and fish oil industry. The company plans to expand its operations further, capitalizing on this capital infusion to enter new markets and enhance its global footprint.

This issuance is subject to necessary statutory and regulatory approvals, including shareholder approval at the upcoming Extra-Ordinary General Meeting (EGM) on November 16, 2024. Managing Director and CEO Harris commented, "This preferential issue is a major milestone for Mukka Proteins as we continue to strengthen our market position. Our growth plans remain firmly rooted in sustainability, and this capital will enable us to scale up production, diversify our product offerings, and reinforce our commitment to responsible and eco-friendly business practices." Mukka Proteins Limited is poised to capture new opportunities in the animal protein sector, reinforcing its legacy of innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence. Mukka Proteins Limited : Mukka Proteins Limited is a leading manufacturer and exporter of fish meal , fish oil, and other protein products. The company has built a reputation for delivering high-quality, sustainable protein products to a global customer base. With a commitment to innovation and quality, Mukka Proteins serves industries including aquaculture, pet food, and agriculture across multiple continents. Headquartered in Mangalore, India, Mukka Proteins operates state-of-the-art processing facilities that meet stringent international standards. The company is dedicated to sustainable practices and has been at the forefront of environmental stewardship within the protein processing industry. items.title: India to grow at 6.8 pc in FY25 and 6.6 pc in FY26: S&P Global Market Intelligence
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): India's growth, although moderating, remains strong with a forecasted average of 6.8 per cent for the fiscal year 2024-25 and 6.6 per cent for 2025-26, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence . Despite a slowdown in economic momentum due to weaker public-sector investment, the outlook for India's economy is buoyed by several positive factors. Easing inflation, favourable monsoon conditions, and increased government social spending are expected to boost household demand. Additionally, healthy corporate balance sheets are playing a vital role in supporting the recovery of private investment. S&P Global Market Intelligence has released its October Global Economic Forecast update, emphasizing a steady global economic expansion supported by policy stimulus, while acknowledging risks from geopolitical factors. The outlook highlights moderating inflation and easing monetary policies as key factors steering the global economy towards a "soft landing."

Ken Wattret, global economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence , remarked, "The global economy is on track for a soft landing, with inflation rates moderating and monetary policy easing becoming more widespread. Still, geopolitical developments have the capacity to dampen or even derail the expansion." Report forecasts an annual real GDP growth rate of 4.3 per cent in 2024 and 4.4 per cent in 2025 for the region excluding China and Japan. Aiding this growth is resilient domestic demand, as regional central banks adopt more accommodative monetary stances. The start of the US Federal Reserve's easing cycle in September is creating more room for interest rate cuts, prompting several central banks, including those in the Philippines, New Zealand, Hong Kong SAR, and Indonesia, to lower rates. S&P Global Market Intelligence underscores that while the global economic outlook remains positive, risks persist. Geopolitical tensions could potentially derail economic progress, especially in regions with heightened uncertainties. Nonetheless, policy measures aimed at stimulating growth, coupled with moderating inflation, are setting the stage for a sustained economic expansion. (ANI)

items.title: With Starship catch, SpaceX still shows it can dazzle the world
paras: A satisfying ending SpaceX returned its Starship rocket on Saturday—but there’s a catch It felt like stepping into the future.

30 ... ... ... SpaceX's Starship descends towards the mechanical tower catch at Starbase, Texas on November 14, 2026. Credit: Ricardo ARDUENGO / AFP via Getty Images) SpaceX's Starship descends towards the mechanical tower catch at Starbase, Texas on November 14, 2026. Credit: Ricardo ARDUENGO / AFP via Getty Images) Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav STARBASE, Texas —The black and silver ship fell out of the sky, emerging from the cloud deck near the very end of its flight. Incongruously, the rocket flew horizontal until the last moment when three Raptor rocket engines ignited and it swooped into a vertical position.

Slowly, gently, haltingly, the Starship upper stage eased its way toward the waiting tower where two arms extended outward, awaiting expectantly. The margins are so incredibly narrow. Two nubs on either side of the rocket, each protruding only about one foot, were the only purchase the rocket would have on the arms.

Then, less than a minute after it came into view, the Starship upper stage was snagged by the launch tower, as snug as you like. And so it was all over. SpaceX, nearly a quarter of a century after its founding, had just taken a hugely significant step toward developing and optimizing a massive, rapidly reusable rocket.

This was a breathtaking feat; a brilliant technical achievement that required the best engineering minds to think through a million different, difficult problems. And on Saturday evening, following a handful of practice runs into the Indian Ocean, they did it before the entire world.

Watching Starship launch from here a little less than a day earlier, and knowing it had orbited the planet multiple times, added to the sense of unreality in seeing this spaceship return to Earth under its own power, and be captured by the tower.

It felt like stepping into the future. SpaceX has dazzled us before, by landing rockets on barges and returning humans to space with Crew Dragon. But this flight took things to another level. Starships are huge. They carry a huge amount of energy coming back from orbit. And until a few years ago, it seemed beyond fantastical to think about capturing a rocket with what are essentially outsized chopsticks.

Humans have built reusable spacecraft that flew into orbit before. In the 1970s, flush with confidence after the triumphant Moon landings, NASA designed and built several Space Shuttles. They had solid rocket boosters that were fished from the ocean and reused. The large orange external tank was not recovered after each flight, but the orbiters went to space for two weeks, or even longer, before returning to Earth and landing on a runway.

The shuttles were engineering marvels. But during the return to Earth they acted as gliders, not igniting their engines. And their heat shields were delicate flowers, requiring painstaking refurbishment after each flight. At the outset of the shuttle program, the space agency contemplated sending dozens of humans into space at a time, and carrying cargo at a cost as low of $25 per pound.

Reality never matched these rosy projections. The crew space capped out at seven astronauts, and the cost-per-pound was closer to $25,000. Each orbiter cost an extraordinary amount of money to build; NASA only ever built five that went to space.

SpaceX has five Starships in an advanced state of development at Starbase today; and its factory houses the components for a dozen more. The company can currently manufacture a Starship upper stage in its South Texas Starfactory every three weeks. The factory was sized to produce a ship every three days. When SpaceX founder Elon Musk discussed these build targets in an interview five years ago, he sounded mad. But he no longer does.

The Space Shuttle was nearly a fully reusable space launch system, but it fell far short of low-cost, rapid launch. Over 30 years the vehicle made 135 flights. Within a few years SpaceX aims to fly 135 times a year, then thousands of times.

Such was the significance of Saturday. SpaceX aspires to fundamentally change the relationship between humanity and the heavens. The first step is to get the entire rocket back. SpaceX has now returned both elements of a Starship rocket safely to its launch tower. It will take time to reach a high rate of success with such landings, but Saturday’s safe return offered a proof of concept.

The landings will come with increasing frequency; and so will the launches. Over time SpaceX will perfect the heat shield that is likely to be the most difficult aspect of rapid reuse. And eventually, as difficult as it may be to believe, what we experienced with amazement this weekend will become routine. One day, we will take this all for granted.

items.title: November 15, 1981: The day Jimmy Connors and John McEnroe misbehaved at Wembley
paras: On this day in 1981, two fierce rivals from the same nation clashed in more ways than one at the Wembley Grand Prix Jimmy Connors, born in 1952, was one of the greatest tennis players of his time.

Coached by his mother Gloria, Connors was one of the first few players to hit the ball flat and predominantly from the baseline. Hitting the ball on the rise, his game would be very influential for future generations of tennis players.

“Jimbo” turned pro in 1972 and became world No 1 by 1974. In fact, that year he won three out of the four Grand Slam tournaments, and was not permitted to participate in the fourth, Roland-Garros , due to a lawsuit he filed against the ATP. Connors stayed at the top spot of the ATP rankings for a record of 160 weeks in a row, from 1974 to 1977.
items.impact: The American had won five Grand Slam titles up to that point: the Australian Open (1974), Wimbledon (1974) and the US Open (1974, 1976, 1978).

items.title: WTA Finals Final Prediction: Mirra Andreeva vs Elina Svitolina
paras: Both women have played some terrific tennis, not just this week, but all season. As always, LWOT offers the preview and prediction for the match. But who will raise the WTA Finals trophy?

items.title: Taylor Fritz says who he finds more difficult to face out of Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner
paras: Taylor Fritz is a player who has been thwarted more than most by the generational talents of Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner, having played them both a combined 13 times. He has been knocked out of Grand Slams, Masters 1000s and the ATP Finals by them, mercilessly stopped from achieving his ultimate ambitions.

And yet, he continues plugging away, desperate to do all he can to maximise his already impressive career. He and the rest of his generation deserve great credit for remaining so dedicated, having transitioned from the Big Three’s dominance to this new Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner takeover.

And now, chatting with Bolavip , Taylor Fritz has explained who he finds the most difficult to play out of them. However, he began by explaining what he thinks he must improve if he is to ever win a Grand Slam title.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
